- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ 0.33) or neutral (0.00), model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is rising.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model frequently overshoots in next 3–5 days; cap forecast at +3–5% above peak.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-horizon, model often fails to catch momentum; increase forecast slope in second half of horizon.
- Mean reversion bias: if model consistently forecasts above 65–68 over 30d, reduce by 1–2% per 10-day segment unless sentiment supports continuation.
- For 30d horizon, if true outcome exceeds forecast by >2% in first 5 days, assume momentum bias; adjust remaining days downward by 0.5–1% per day.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” (e.g., 0.67 → 0.00 → 0.67), model often misreads trend; use 3-day moving average of sentiment to smooth forecast bias.
